## Candidate Observations

### Observation 1 — Explicit, blanket AI-generated-content ban (policy document)

**File:** [docs/devel/code-provenance.rst, lines 288–349](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/qemu-project-qemu@300438ffbb8d9430cac2fcc15cba6f482b2c0587/-/blob/docs/devel/code-provenance.rst?L288-L349)

The section "Use of AI-generated content" is the primary AI-governance artifact in the repository. Key verbatim text (lines 293–295):

> **Current QEMU project policy is to DECLINE any contributions which are believed to include or derive from AI generated content. This includes ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Llama and similar tools.**

And (lines 297–299):

> **This policy does not apply to other uses of AI, such as researching APIs or algorithms, static analysis, or debugging, provided their output is not included in contributions.**

The policy:
- Names specific tools: GitHub Copilot, OpenAI ChatGPT, Anthropic Claude, Meta Code Llama, and "code/content generation agents which are built on top of such tools."
- Grounds the ban in DCO (Developer's Certificate of Origin) compliance risk, citing unclear copyright/license status of LLM outputs.
- States the project "will decline any contribution if use of AI is either known or **suspected**."
- Includes an "Exceptions" subsection requiring mailing-list discussion before any exception is granted; no exceptions are currently enumerated.
- Notes the policy "may evolve as AI tools mature and the legal situation is clarified."

```

```

### Observation 2 — Mandatory disclosure of AI/LLM use in bug reports (issue template)

**File:** [.gitlab/issue_templates/bug.md, lines 53–58](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/qemu-project-qemu@300438ffbb8d9430cac2fcc15cba6f482b2c0587/-/blob/.gitlab/issue_templates/bug.md?L53-L58)

The "Steps to reproduce" section of the bug template contains (lines 53–57):

```
Note: if this issue was discovered with the assistance of automated
tooling LLM, static analysis, fuzzers), the reporter must disclose
that in the description. The steps to reproduce, and any other findings,
must be fully validated by the user of the tool prior to submission.
```

This is the only contributor-facing instruction file that explicitly names LLMs. It mandates: (a) disclosure if an LLM, static analyzer, or fuzzer assisted discovery, and (b) human validation of all findings before submission. The feature_request template has no equivalent requirement.

No human review step is present. The bot has `pull-requests: write` permission only.
